structured_output.better_next_step_if_any: Name and synchronize the integration branch, repair canonical-scene authority for the selected slice, then prove the Windows Unity runner from the proposed worktree before changing code. Ship NSC-005 only as a no-new-platform manual baseline; use a human-approved NSC-003A movement slice as the first discriminating architecture test. Retain the whole-GDD hash as a fail-closed change alarm with human impact waivers, deferring requirement IDs and coordinator code until an observed failure justifies them.
failure_if_followed: The “thin lane” may consume the remaining window building a driver, journal, preflight, requirement map, manifest generator, writable-provider boundary, and recovery test around a tiny feature.

Selective requirement invalidation can produce false-current evidence when a human impact set omits a cross-cutting requirement or Unity dependency—the exact class of miss demonstrated by the scene relocation.
A writable agent may exceed scope or alter contracts, canon, evidence, external files, or commands because current write boundaries are request metadata, not an implemented enforcement boundary.

A green NSC-005 result could be misrepresented as proof of autonomous Unity delivery even though it avoids Input Actions, packages, scene authoring, serialized integration, build settings, useful dependency readiness, and real spell/restart consumers.
The GDD/task/scene split remains active while the human Play Mode check necessarily uses the scene the GDD calls non-canonical.
Journal, Git, Unity artifacts, merge state, and receipt state can disagree after a crash because storage, atomic transitions, idempotency, and reconciliation semantics are unspecified.
Windows licensing, Editor locking, worktree import/cache cost, or host availability may be discovered only after contract and orchestration work has consumed the one-day budget.
PlayerMana reset and denied-feedback APIs may be reworked when the absent restart orchestrator and actual spells finally establish their integration semantics.
Arbitrary one-day and 90-minute thresholds may approve a slower architecture—or reject a useful one—because no comparable manual baseline exists.
hidden_assumptions: Stable requirement IDs plus human-reviewed impact sets will be complete enough to replace conservative whole-GDD invalidation.
The human process that missed propagation of the authoritative scene move will reliably identify every future requirement/task/surface impact.
A safely contained write-capable worker can be enabled cheaply; both current providers explicitly reject repository writes and approved command execution.
An isolated worktree enforces file and command scope. It provides recovery/isolation, but it is not a security boundary.
A typed manifest proves provenance. Current evidence accepts hand-authored gate claims and a nonempty approver name; typing alone does not authenticate Unity execution or human approval.
A protected integration ref already exists. Frozen HEAD is `provider-adapters`, while local `main` is eight commits behind.
An append-only journal can atomically coordinate Git refs, external Unity results, human decisions, and merge events without compare-and-set or idempotency semantics.
NSC-005 is representative of later Unity work despite having no dependencies or exclusive resources and only in-memory component tests.
Debug-only mana spending is adequate evidence of player-facing denied-cast behavior even though no spell exists.
Human reset validation is executable without adding a reset driver, restart orchestrator, debug control, or scene change.
The Windows Unity host, license, project lock, and fresh-worktree import latency will fit the proposed schedule.
Eight role-separated reviews provide strong independent support for the cure, although all eight current review JSONs identify the same provider and model family.
ignored_minority_arguments: The YAGNI/no-new-platform argument was diluted: record the first lifecycle manually and implement coordinator code only for a failure actually observed. The synthesis instead requires a driver, journal, preflight, manifest, and deliberate interruption immediately.

The workflow review required compare-and-set transitions, idempotency keys, reconciliation against real refs, and authenticated authority. The synthesis reduces this to an unspecified append-only journal and receipt.

The workflow review recommended fixing canonical-scene split-brain before NSC-005. The synthesis defers the migration even though NSC-005's contract cites the deleted scene and its human gate uses the surviving scene.

The Unity review stressed one-host Editor locking, import/cache strategy, exact committed-scene inspection, and post-rebase validation. “One worktree plus clean runner” does not resolve those production constraints.

The reliability review questioned correlated semantic review and unnormalized cost evidence. The synthesis still uses a five-versus-three reviewer split when choosing the first slice and supplies an ungrounded throughput threshold.

The five-reviewer movement case was explicitly overridden. A reduced NSC-003A is harder, but it is materially more discriminating and advances six direct dependents; NSC-005's two dependents also require NSC-003, so NSC-005 unlocks nothing by itself.
structured_output.reason: The synthesis's diagnosis largely holds: the repository is an audit platform without a delivery transaction, and its human, Git, Unity, bounded-repair, and clean-tree boundaries should survive. Its concrete prescription does not yet hold. At frozen commit `9f2485d`, the proposed “minimum” introduces several unimplemented control-plane abstractions and weakens conservative canon handling before proving either enforcement or impact completeness. Its chosen NSC-005 experiment is too easy and too artificial to distinguish architectural leverage from an ordinary manual coding workflow. This is material enough to require revision, but not enough to reject the delivery-first direction entirely.
structured_output.strongest_counter_case: The synthesis has recreated platform-first development in miniature. NSC-005 is a two-script component change around five in-memory tests (`Tasks/NSC-005.yaml`; `PlayerManaPlayModeTests.cs`), exercised through `DebugManaSpendControl`, with no production spell, restart orchestrator, scene change, build scene, lock, or standalone dependency unlock. Yet the slice demands requirement revisioning, a preflight, write containment, checkpoint/resume machinery, deliberate interruption, typed evidence, two exact-commit validations, and telemetry. Success would prove little about the architecture's real risks; failure could come from new plumbing or the untested Windows host rather than agent capability. A safer, faster architecture is initially procedural: a named human-owned integration branch, one manually created worktree, one ordinary coding worker under external containment, Git commits as recovery, the existing clean Unity runner, external XML/logs, one human review, and a short receipt. Keep the full-GDD hash as a change alarm and allow a reviewed no-code rebind for unaffected work. After a no-platform baseline, use a clarified NSC-003A movement slice to test real Input Actions, committed-scene integration, human feel, repair, and downstream value. Only automate the lifecycle step that actually fails repeatedly.
synthesis_weaknesses: It conflates making a record stale with rerunning every test. A whole-GDD hash can remain a conservative change alarm while a human impact review rebinds unaffected evidence; stable requirement infrastructure is not required yet.

Selective invalidation is riskier than acknowledged. `current_conformance.py:164-198` is overbroad but fail-closed; reviewed impact sets would be underbroad unless completeness is independently proven.

The first slice is not discriminating. `NSC-005` has no dependencies or exclusive resources; its tests instantiate only `PlayerMana`; the proposed visible behavior is driven by a debug-only control; and `EditorBuildSettings.asset:7` contains no build scene.

It avoids the architecture's hardest Unity boundaries: Input Actions, builder and serialized-scene changes, `.meta` identity, packages, project settings, real integration consumers, and meaningful dependency propagation.

Deferring scene-authority repair is internally inconsistent. `Tasks/NSC-005.yaml:83-85` cites the deleted scene, the GDD calls the surviving scene non-canonical, while the human readability gate must open that surviving scene.

The proposed path-only preflight is weaker than the synthesis's own claimed preflight. Existence does not prove canonical identity, GUID agreement, serialized references, package compatibility, Build Settings, or semantic currency.
The write-capability boundary is unspecified. `OpenAICodexProvider` and `ClaudeCodeProvider` reject writes/commands; `WriteBoundaries` is not used by an executor to enforce filesystem access.

The lifecycle model is incomplete: `merged` precedes post-merge validation and receipt publication, but there is no explicit integrated-pending-validation or verified-delivered state. Journal location, atomicity, and crash recovery are undefined.

The receipt remains an authority assertion unless the runner emits it through a trusted channel and human approval comes from protected review/merge provenance. Current `approved_by` validation checks only for nonempty text.
The exact integration target is unresolved: repository decisions say `main` defines Done, but frozen HEAD is a different branch and `main` is behind.
The success test's human reset check has no runtime trigger. The existing debug component exposes only spend, and there is no restart orchestrator or reset button/key.

Mandatory post-merge Unity reruns may double the slowest step unnecessarily. If a protected fast-forward or merge produces an identical relevant tree, deterministic tree equality can justify reusing candidate evidence.
The one-day, two-repair, 90-minute targets have no baseline and cannot establish causal throughput improvement.
Role-separated consensus is correlated evidence, not eight independent architecture experiments; every current review used the same provider/model family.
what_would_change_my_mind: A demonstrated externally enforced writable sandbox limits the worker to the selected worktree and approved commands, denies task/canon/evidence paths, and proves containment independently of agent claims.
A no-change run proves the exact Windows Unity host, license, worktree path, Editor-lock policy, import/cache strategy, XML production, and clean-tree checks with measured latency.
The integration ref is explicitly named and protected, candidate-to-integration identity is defined, and human approval comes from authenticated review/merge provenance rather than a JSON name field.

The journal has a specified location and legal transition table, idempotency keys, crash-window handling, and recovery tests for commit-before-journal, merge-before-receipt, and validation-before-publication failures.
Requirement-impact handling defaults fail-closed for unmapped changes and is tested against the observed scene move plus cross-cutting Input Action, package, prefab, and ProjectSettings changes.
A direct manual baseline and the proposed lane are measured comparably for wall time, human time, Unity time, repairs, and defects.
The same lane delivers a clarified movement/scene-integrating slice without new orchestration code after NSC-005, demonstrating that NSC-005 was not a one-off false green.
Canonical-scene authority is corrected before scene-dependent human validation, and the selected contract retains explicit proof of the actual serialized UI wiring.
